Hrm, I think (hope!) those include guards won't be triggered often for PRs. For this reason, it might be preferable to have them be checked as little as possible during normal development.
Especially, I was thinking people might want to add includes during dev to 'just make something work temporarily' without needing to worry about the include guards. Most times they'll probably use `dev_mode=yes`, but perhaps sometimes they won't.

However, I could really see it going either way. If you feel strongly about this, I'm happy to adjust.

> I would personally tend towards SCU_BUILD_ENABLED as we tend to have e.g. ANDROID_ENABLED, DEV_ENABLED etc as a convention (maybe we might want to use e.g. SCU_BUILD in a macro in future or something).

Makes sense to me, I'll adjust on the next rebase.

> Also just to check, my python-fu isn't strong, is there any possibility that we could end up defining this more than once in the same environment? (I.e. could the compiler command line end up having lots of similar defines?)

I think `self.Append(CPPDEFINES=["SCU_BUILD"])` _will_ be called more than once for the same env, because `add_source_files` is often called more than once on the same env. I don't think it should be a problem though if SCONS de-duplicates cpp defines.
What's notable is that `SCU_BUILD_ENABLED` propagates to other classes (that aren't SCU-ified), but only if others _are_ SCU-ified in the same env. So that's probably acceptable.

I see no reason to exclude debug/dev builds from these assertions; that's arguably where they'd be most useful! If a user really wants compilation to "just work," it's far more reasonable for them to either make this conditional universally `true`, or comment out a specific assertion.
```suggestion
#ifndef SCU_BUILD_ENABLED
```
